title: Polynomial localizations over a regular local base reflect maximal-ideal order
statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian regular local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-regular-scheme]. Let $s\ge0$, $P=R[Y_1,\ldots,Y_s]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and let $\mathfrak q\subset P$ be a prime ideal whose inverse image in $R$ is $\mathfrak m$. Put $S=P_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak qS$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then $S$ is regular local and, for the natural map $j:R\to S$, one has
$$j^{-1}(\mathfrak n^a)=\mathfrak m^a\qquad(a\in\mathbf N).$$
In particular $j$ preserves maximal-ideal orders, where $\operatorname{ord}_J(u)=\sup\{a\in\mathbf N:u\in J^a\}$, valued in $\mathbf N\cup\{\infty\}$. Empty variable lists and the zero element are included.

source.place: Agent synthesis of Tag 031E (lemma-flat-over-regular-with-regular-fibre), its parameter-generating proof, and Tag 00NO (lemma-regular-graded). The polynomial-local order reflection is the consequence of extending base parameters and the canonical graded polynomial map, not the verbatim assertion of either tag. Also Hironaka (1970), proof of Lemma 14, p.169, the contraction of maximal-ideal powers along polynomial localizations.

proof.text: Write $k=R/\mathfrak m$ and $L=S/\mathfrak n$. Since $P$ is a finite-type $R$-algebra, it is Noetherian, and its localization $S$ is Noetherian. The prime-localization definition gives that $S$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$. Its contraction to $R$ is $\mathfrak m$: a base element outside $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak q\cap R$ is inverted in $S$, while elements of $\mathfrak m$ map into $\mathfrak n$. The polynomial projection is flat, and the affine spectrum stalk-map identification identifies its map at $\mathfrak q$ with the map on local rings $R_{\mathfrak m}\to P_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat by the definition of a flat morphism. Identify $R_{\mathfrak m}$ with $R$ by $r/t\mapsto rt^{-1}$ (every $t\notin\mathfrak m$ is a unit). Thus $j:R\to S$ is a flat local map. The residue map $k\to L$ is injective, since its kernel is $(j^{-1}(\mathfrak n))/\mathfrak m=0$.

source.place: Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence); morphisms.tex Tag 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize), polynomial projection and its local rings

proof.text:
Reduction of polynomial coefficients induces $P/\mathfrak mP\simeq k[Y_1,\ldots,Y_s]$: the kernel consists exactly of polynomials all of whose coefficients lie in $\mathfrak m$. Since $\mathfrak mP\subseteq\mathfrak q$, the quotient-localization isomorphism identifies
$$F=S/\mathfrak mS\simeq k[Y_1,\ldots,Y_s]_{\overline{\mathfrak q}}.$$
The polynomial ring over the field $k$ is regular, hence $F$ is regular local, including when $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ is not maximal. Regularity ascent along the flat local map of Step 1 now proves that $S$ is regular local.

Put $d=\dim R$ and $e=\dim F$. The flat height formula, applied to the maximal ideals of the Noetherian local rings $R$ and $S$, gives $\dim S=d+e$. Choose $d$ generators $x_1,\ldots,x_d$ of $\mathfrak m$, and choose lifts $y_1,\ldots,y_e\in\mathfrak n$ of $e$ generators of the maximal ideal of $F$. These choices are available by the definition of regular local rings. Then $j(x_1),\ldots,j(x_d),y_1,\ldots,y_e$ generate $\mathfrak n$: subtracting a linear combination of the $y_i$ puts any element of $\mathfrak n$ in $\mathfrak mS$, which is generated by the $j(x_i)$. Their classes span $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2$ over $L$. The regular-local cotangent dimension criterion gives dimension $d+e$ for this space, so this spanning list of $d+e$ vectors is a basis. Similarly the classes of the $x_i$ form a $k$-basis of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$.

source.place: Tag 00ON (lemma-dimension-base-fibre-equals-total); parameter-generating proof of Tag 031E; regular local cotangent criterion

proof.text:
Apply the canonical regular-local graded criterion to $R$ and $S$. Using the bases of Step 3 and the symmetric-algebra polynomial identification, it gives
$$\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}R\simeq k[X_1,\ldots,X_d],\qquad
\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak n}S\simeq L[X_1,\ldots,X_d,Z_1,\ldots,Z_e],$$
where $X_i$ represents $x_i$ downstairs and $j(x_i)$ upstairs, and $Z_i$ represents $y_i$. Explicitly, to transport the stated symmetric-algebra identification from a standard free module to either cotangent space, apply the symmetric-algebra universal property to its basis isomorphism and inverse; the induced maps compose to the identity because they agree with the identity on all generators. The induced graded map $\operatorname{gr}(j)$ therefore sends each $X_i$ to the same $X_i$ and each coefficient through $k\hookrightarrow L$. It is injective: a nonzero polynomial has a nonzero coefficient at some $X$-monomial, and that coefficient stays nonzero in $L$; adjoining the $Z$ variables does not identify monomials. This argument identifies the actual induced map, rather than only abstractly isomorphic graded rings.

source.place: Tag 00NO (lemma-regular-graded), canonical parameter map in its proof; Section 00DM (section-tensor-algebra)

proof.text: Prove $j^{-1}(\mathfrak n^a)=\mathfrak m^a$ by induction on $a$. For $a=0$ both ideals are the whole ring. Suppose the equality holds at $a$, and let $j(r)\in\mathfrak n^{a+1}$. Since $\mathfrak n^{a+1}\subseteq\mathfrak n^a$, the induction hypothesis gives $r\in\mathfrak m^a$. The degree-$a$ class of $r$ is sent by $\operatorname{gr}(j)$ to zero, so Step 4 gives $r\in\mathfrak m^{a+1}$. Conversely $j(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak n$ implies $j(\mathfrak m^{a+1})\subseteq\mathfrak n^{a+1}$ by multiplying generators and adding. This completes the induction.

source.place: Tag 00NO (lemma-regular-graded), elementary filtered consequence of the injection established in Step 4

proof.text: For every $u\in R$, Step 5 identifies the two subsets of $\mathbf N$ defining its orders: $\{a:u\in\mathfrak m^a\}=\{a:j(u)\in\mathfrak n^a\}$. Their suprema in $\mathbf N\cup\{\infty\}$ are equal. If $u=0$, both sets are all of $\mathbf N$, so both orders are $\infty$. Empty variable lists and $d=0$ or $e=0$ require no changes: the parameter bases and corresponding polynomial variable lists can be empty throughout.

lean.statement: theorem polynomialLocalization_orderReflection (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsRegularLocalRing R] (s : ℕ) (q : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin s) R)) [q.IsPrime] (hq : q.comap (algebraMap R (MvPolynomial (Fin s) R)) = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) : IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime q) ∧ (∀ a : ℕ, (q.map (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin s) R) (Localization.AtPrime q)) ^ a).comap (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime q)) = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R ^ a) ∧ (∀ r : R, adicOrder (q.map (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin s) R) (Localization.AtPrime q))) (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime q) r) = adicOrder (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) r)
